newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-DENNIS COOK HOMERS IN NINTH AS MARLINS NIP CARDS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DENNIS COOK HOMERS IN NINTH AS MARLINS NIP CARDS.

text.p: Reliever Dennis Cook's "blind luck" home run with two out in the top of the ninth inning was the difference as the Florida Marlins survived a late rally to edge the St. Louis Cardinals 5-4 Friday.

With the Marlins leading 4-2 in the ninth, Cook drove a 3-2 pitch from reliever T. J. Mathews over the left-centre field fence. It was his second major-league homer and first since he hit one off the Dodgers' Fernando Valenzuela on May 19, 1990.
"I was fortunate to go up and hit," said Cook. "I was just looking to get good wood on it. It was just blind luck. Anytime a pitcher hits one, that's exactly what it is."

Florida closer Robb Nen issued consecutive walks to open the ninth before giving up a two-out, two-run single to pinch-hitter Tom Lampkin. But Delino DeShields grounded out to end the game for Nenn's 26th save in 31 opportunities.
Livan Hernandez (4-0) won his fourth straight start, giving up two runs and five hits over 6 2/3 innings. Cook struck out two of four batters without allowing a hit.
Charles Johnson had a two-run homer and a one-run single for Florida. Royce Clayton hit a two-run homer off Hernandez in the seventh.
Alan Benes (9-9) surrendered four runs and eight hits over eight innings for the Cardinals, who have lost three straight.

In San Diego, Carl Everett hit a two-out, two-run single -- the only hit in a three-run eighth inning that saw two rare errors by Padre third baseman Ken Caminiti -- as the New York Mets rallied for their eighth win in nine games, 4-2.
It was the second game in a row that Everett drove in the game-winner.
The Mets stayed even with Florida for the National League wild card, 5 1/2 games behind Atlanta in the East.

In Cincinnati, Jeff Blauser hit his fourth career grand slam and John Smoltz fired a two-hitter as the Atlanta Braves continued their mastery of the Reds with a 7-3 victory, spoiling the first game for interim manager Jack McKeon.
Andruw Jones, Chipper Jones and Fred McGriff added solo homers for the Braves, who have won all six games from the Reds this season by a combined score of 48-14.

Smoltz (9-9) gave up a single and a three-run homer in the fifth but retired 12 of the last 13 batters for his third win over the Reds this year. He walked four and recorded a season-high 10 strikeouts.
McKeon was named Reds interim manager before the game following the firing of Ray Knight.

At Colorado, Dante Bichette's three-run homer keyed a four-run first inning and Frank Castillo pitched 8 1/3 innings to defeat his former club as the Rockies routed the Chicago Cubs 9-3 for their third straight victory.

After Sammy Sosa homered in the top of the first to give the Cubs a 1-0 lead, Bichette's 16th homer, a 445-foot (135 metres) blast, gave Colorado a 3-1 lead and Vinny Castilla followed with his 28th of the season. Castilla is one homer behind teammate Larry Walker for the league lead.
Castillo (7-9), acquired from Chicago on July 15, allowed three runs and 11 hits to post his first win for the Rockies.

In Houston, Darryl Kile pitched a seven-hitter to become the National League's second 14-game winner and Jeff Bagwell hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the fifth as the Astros beat the Montreal Expos 5-2 for their seventh straight win.

Kile (14-3), who tossed his second complete game against the Expos in six days, allowed two runs -- one earned -- with eight strikeouts to win his seventh consecutive decision. It also was Kile's career-high fifth complete game of the season.
Kile, who joined Atlanta's Greg Maddux as the only 14-game winners in the N.L., retired the final 14 batters.
Jeff Juden (11-4) took the loss as Houston improved to 12-3 since the All-Star break.

In Los Angeles, Chan Ho Park went a career-high eight innings to win his fourth straight start and Mike Piazza and Eric Karros hit three-run homers and knocked in four each, powering the Dodgers past the Philadelphia Phillies 8-1.

Park (9-5) gave up one run and four hits, walked four and struck out four. During his four-game winning streak, Park has allowed just seven runs and 20 hits over 27 2/3 innings, walking eight and fanning 23.

In San Francisco, Jason Schmidt allowed one run over seven innings and Jermaine Allensworth went 3-for-3 with two RBI as the Pittsburgh Pirates snapped a three-game losing streak with a 5-2 victory over the Giants.
Schmidt (5-6), who was winless in three starts following a three-game winning streak, gave up five hits with four walks and six strikeouts. Rich Loiselle worked a perfect ninth for his 15th save.
Kevin Polcovich added a solo homer and scored three times for Pittsburgh, 9-1 in its last 10 games at San Francisco.
Giants superstar Barry Bonds hit a solo homer, his 27th of the year and 361st of his career to equal San Francisco native Joe DiMaggio for 43rd on the all-time list.
